No missing-emissions mass bound assigned.

column3: Manufacturing industries and construction - all other
column13: NO LONGER THE GAP IT WAS: the rc46 activation put the measured HDIP coal-by-consumer series INTO the reference - brick-kiln coal 2.78 and cement-sector coal 10.80 Mt through the industrial_solid_fuels_1a2 scope gate - and the supply-consumption identity (imports+production exhausts the consumer columns to ~0.5 kt in 8 of 9 years) closed the old industrial-coal/petcoke refusal: 'other industrial coal' is definitionally ~zero and petcoke rides the Comtrade lane. EDGAR puts Pakistani industrial combustion near 44 Mt CO2e against the engine's 22.58, and the ~15.9 Mt benchmark residual (outputs/industry_fuel_ledger_2024.csv) is now benchmark disagreement over an exhaustive consumer series, bounded but not decomposable: its remaining named claimants are the cement transferred-intensity model's EXCESS over the measured series (+1.2 to +4.9 Mt, configuration cement_kiln_fuel_in_scope) and the process-bagasse ceiling (0.39 Mt). The brick and captive screenings retired at rc47 Wave 0 - superseded_by_reference_stream in the fuel ledger; adding either to a reference that books the measured series would double-count, which is exactly what their configurations briefly did. What would still move this category is a Pakistani kiln heat-intensity audit (to settle the cement excess) and industrial fuel by type beyond the Statistical Supplement's consumer split - HDIP Pakistan Energy Yearbook (paid, eyb@hdip.gov.pk) or OCAC (members-only). No missing-emissions mass bound assigned.

The fuel is IDENTIFIED AND PRICED, the scope is not attributed: the OCAC customer bridge assigns 120,758 t of military/government jet fuel, 4,542 t of 100LL and 12,282 t of unresolved government JP-1 - about 0.435 Mt CO2, priced as memo rows in outputs/aviation_totals_fy2023_24.csv, restated as the observed-unallocated account outputs/aviation_unallocated_fuel_fy2023_24.csv (each tonne with an evidence class, a disposition and a named closer), and as three independent national configurations (military_government_in_scope, general_aviation_in_scope, unresolved_jp1_in_scope; the split of one lumped axis) - but no record attributes the activity between military operations and civil government use, and IPCC reports military aviation under 1A5b. See aviation-1a5b-scope. No missing-emissions mass bound assigned.

SCREENED, not estimated: the two blockers the earlier row named - a marine factor choice and a domestic/foreign boundary review - are made in sectors/transport/navigation_screen.py, and every held OCAC edition's Domestic Bunkers row is converted in outputs/transport_navigation_screen_2024.csv (3,054 t HSD in the FY2023-24 reference year, 0.0098 Mt CO2e on IPCC Tables 3.5.2/3.5.3). Would be a memo item if it were estimated. NOT to be taken from the 'Overseas/Export' line of OGRA Table 2.1: that line is exported furnace-oil CARGO, not fuel bunkered at Pakistani ports - 1.01 Mt for FY2023-24 against 1.11 Mt of furnace-oil exports reported for calendar 2024. The one figure that does exist is Pakistan's own: BTR1 books 1.A.3.d.i international marine bunkers at 0.0393 Mt CO2, 0.040 Mt CO2e, for 2020-21 (sources/UNFCCC/btr1_2024.txt line 843) - two orders of magnitude below the roughly 3 Mt the OGRA line would give, which is why the trap matters. An earlier version of this row said Pakistan had no formal bunkering market until 2026 and let that carry the absence; a market's absence is not the absence of fuel delivered, and the national submission books some. Recorded so nobody builds the sector on that line, and so nobody reads this as nothing to estimate. No missing-emissions mass bound assigned.

column3: Air pollutants - power generation, as actually emitted
column13: Needs control-device inventory and performance by unit: which plants have precipitators or flue-gas desulphurisation and at what removal efficiency. The five NEPRA Licensees HSE Performance Evaluation Reports were fetched and audited in August 2026: they publish no per-plant equipment or emissions, but their questionnaire scores licensees on air-quality controls and on submitting environmental monitoring reports - so the data exists at NEPRA as unpublished licensee submissions, and the route is a request to its HSE department. Applying a removal rate without it would be inventing the number that matters most, since it spans an order of magnitude between uncontrolled and well-controlled. No missing-emissions mass bound assigned.
